section: Investigation of single additive ZPS on performance of copper foil > ABSTRACT
text: This work investigated the influence of Sodium 3- (benzothiazole-2 -ylthio)- 1- propanesulfonate (ZPS) as a single additive on performance of copper foil. Electrochemical analysis indicates that ZPS is of accelerating effect during electroplating. Chronoamperometry and ex situ SEM confirm that Copper growth obeys 3D diffusioncontrolled instantaneous nucleation and growth process, with ZPS significantly increasing the density of active sites.

section: Investigation of single additive ZPS on performance of copper foil > ABSTRACT
text: Chronoamperometry and ex situ SEM confirm that Copper growth obeys 3D diffusioncontrolled instantaneous nucleation and growth process, with ZPS significantly increasing the density of active sites. A comprehensive theoretical framework combining density functional theory calculations, molecula dynamics simulations, and in situ infrared spectroscopy elucidates an adsorption-capturing acceleration mechanism: ZPS can adsorb on copper surface and “catch” free Cu 2+ to the active sites to accelerate the electrochemical reduction process coupled with adsorbed Cl −.

section: Investigation of single additive ZPS on performance of copper foil > ABSTRACT
text: A comprehensive theoretical framework combining density functional theory calculations, molecula dynamics simulations, and in situ infrared spectroscopy elucidates an adsorption-capturing acceleration mechanism: ZPS can adsorb on copper surface and “catch” free Cu 2+ to the active sites to accelerate the electrochemical reduction process coupled with adsorbed Cl −. Furthermore, a Turing oscillation growth model, supported by finite element simulations and AFM analysis, is proposed to describe the morphological evolution, wherein ZPS preferentially accumulates at valley regions, improving surface flatness through cyclic peak-valley transfer, though with inherently limited ultimate smoothing.

section: Investigation of single additive ZPS on performance of copper foil > ABSTRACT
text: Furthermore, a Turing oscillation growth model, supported by finite element simulations and AFM analysis, is proposed to describe the morphological evolution, wherein ZPS preferentially accumulates at valley regions, improving surface flatness through cyclic peak-valley transfer, though with inherently limited ultimate smoothing. Structurally, XRD shows ZPS promotes Cu (220) orientation, while HRTEM confirms the presence of twin boundaries, and lattice fringe measurements reveal a transition from (111)-dominated to (220)-dominated regions upon ZPS addition.

section: Investigation of single additive ZPS on performance of copper foil > ABSTRACT
text: Structurally, XRD shows ZPS promotes Cu (220) orientation, while HRTEM confirms the presence of twin boundaries, and lattice fringe measurements reveal a transition from (111)-dominated to (220)-dominated regions upon ZPS addition. Electron backscatter diffraction (EBSD) further indicates grain refinement (mean size from 3.29 μm to 2.60 μm) and increased twin-boundary density, which contribute to strengthening via Hall-Petch and dislocation-blocking effects. In terms of performance, ZPS improves surface morphology and reduces roughness.

section: Investigation of single additive ZPS on performance of copper foil > ABSTRACT
text: In terms of performance, ZPS improves surface morphology and reduces roughness. Mechanical properties are optimized at 30 mg/L ZPS, with tensile strength reaching 331 MPa and elongation 3.78 %. Finite-element simulation of high frequency signal transmission demonstrates that the lowered roughness effectively mitigates the skin effect, reducing signal loss. Overall, this work provides a comprehensive mechanistic understanding of ZPS and dem onstrates its potential as a single additive for producing high-performance electrolytic copper foils.

section: Investigation of single additive ZPS on performance of copper foil > 1. Introduction
text: Copper clad laminate (CCL) is one of the key materials in PCB, consisting of copper foil and substrate, among which copper foil directly affects the electrical performance and mechanical performance of PCB [3]. There are two methods to prepare copper foil in industry, namely, electrolytic copper foil and rolled copper foil, among which rolled copper foil is fabricated by rolling and compressing pure copper [4]. However, the production cost of rolled copper foil is expensive and the thickness is limited [5].

section: Investigation of single additive ZPS on performance of copper foil > 1. Introduction
text: However, the production cost of rolled copper foil is expensive and the thickness is limited [5]. In contrast, electrolyte copper foil is cost-friendly and suitable for scale-up production [6]. In widely-used acid sulfate copper electroplating process, free Cu^2+ obtain electrons and is reduced on Ti cathode surface to form copper foil [7,8]. However, it is hard to directly prepare satisfied electrolyte copper foil from acid sulfate copper solution without the aid of additives to satisfy the fabrication requirement of advanced electronic products [9].

section: Investigation of single additive ZPS on performance of copper foil > 2.4. Electroplating
text: Electroplating was carried out in circulating cell with volume of 1 L and the circulating rate was 3 L/min. Phosphor copper plate was used as anode, while polished titanium plate was used as cathode. Before carrying out electroplating, titanium substrate was immersed in acetone at ultrasonic condition for 10 min to degrease oil and laterally was activated by 10 wt. %H_2S0_4. The current density used for electroplating was 30 A/dm2 at 298 K for 40 s and the thickness of prepared copper foil was about 4.5 μm.

text: The influence of ZPS on grain size was investigated by EBSD. The Image Quality (IQ) maps (d2, e2) show that the addition of ZPS reduces the grain size and induces high density boundaries. Specifically, the mean grain size decreases from 3.29 μm to 2.60 μm (d4, e4). According to Hall-Petch strengthening mechanism, grain boundaries act as strong barriers to dislocation motion. Grain refinement dramatically increases the total grain boundary area, leading to sharp increase in strength. As a result, the improved grain boundaries density by ZPS is conducive for enhancing mechanical performance.

section: Investigation of single additive ZPS on performance of copper foil > 4. Conclusion
text: In this study, additive Sodium 3-(benzothiazole-2-ylthio)-1-pro panesulfonate (ZPS) has been systematically investigated for copper foil electrodeposition. Cyclic voltammetry and electrochemical impedance spectra indicate that ZPS is of accelerating effect during electroplating. Chronoamperometry and ex situ SEM shows that the 3D diffusion controlled instantaneous nucleation and growth model is not changed but the active sites are increased by ZPS.

section: Investigation of single additive ZPS on performance of copper foil > 4. Conclusion
text: Chronoamperometry and ex situ SEM shows that the 3D diffusion controlled instantaneous nucleation and growth model is not changed but the active sites are increased by ZPS. Theoretical analysis suggests that ZPS can adsorb on copper surface and catch free Cu ^2 + by -SO 3 − to accelerate the electro-reduction coupled with adsorbed Cl − through “bridging effect”. Adsorption-capturing accelerating mechanism was proposed. Molecular dynamics simulation and in situ infrared spectroscopy verify the improved adsorption property of ZPS with increased cathodic polarization.

section: Investigation of single additive ZPS on performance of copper foil > 4. Conclusion
text: Molecular dynamics simulation and in situ infrared spectroscopy verify the improved adsorption property of ZPS with increased cathodic polarization. A Turing oscillation growth model, validated by finite-element simulation and AFM, reveals that ZPS accumulates in valleys to locally accelerate growth, improving flatness via cyclic peakvalley transfer, but the smoothing effect is ultimately constrained by this oscillation.

section: Investigation of single additive ZPS on performance of copper foil > 4. Conclusion
text: A Turing oscillation growth model, validated by finite-element simulation and AFM, reveals that ZPS accumulates in valleys to locally accelerate growth, improving flatness via cyclic peakvalley transfer, but the smoothing effect is ultimately constrained by this oscillation. Structural characterization demonstrates that ZPS selectively promotes the Cu (220) crystal orientation and suppresses the (200) plane, while HRTEM directly visualizes twin boundaries, with lattice fringes showing a shift from (111) to (220) in twin-vicinity regions upon ZPS addition.

section: Investigation of single additive ZPS on performance of copper foil > 4. Conclusion
text: Structural characterization demonstrates that ZPS selectively promotes the Cu (220) crystal orientation and suppresses the (200) plane, while HRTEM directly visualizes twin boundaries, with lattice fringes showing a shift from (111) to (220) in twin-vicinity regions upon ZPS addition. EBSD confirms grain refinement (mean grain size reduced from 3.29 μm to 2.60 μm) and a marked increase in twinboundary density, which together enhance mechanical performance through Hall-Petch strengthening and dislocation obstruction.

section: Investigation of single additive ZPS on performance of copper foil > 4. Conclusion
text: EBSD confirms grain refinement (mean grain size reduced from 3.29 μm to 2.60 μm) and a marked increase in twinboundary density, which together enhance mechanical performance through Hall-Petch strengthening and dislocation obstruction. text: Regarding copper foil performance, surface morphology is noticeably improved, while the optimal mechanical properties are achieved at 30 mg/L ZPS, yielding a tensile strength of 331 MPa and elongation of 3.78 %, attributed to grain refinement and twin-boundary strengthening. Collectively, this work not only establishes ZPS as an effective single additive for industrial copper foil production but also advances the fundamental understanding of additive-induced structure-property relationships, offering a solid foundation for future additive design and process optimization.
